algorithm: PD controller (fixed spring-damper set-points for a clenched-fist grasp; K = 0.4 Nm/rad, B = 0.005 Nms/rad)
hand: Shadow Hand (custom-modeled 35-DOF arm+hand test rig, built once in MJCF and replicated per engine; not a distributed/released asset)
arm: integrated with the hand as a single 35-DOF Shadow-Hand-modeled arm/hand system; no separate arm model
sim: MuJoCo (Euler and RK integrators), Bullet (+ experimental Featherstone/BulletMB variant), ODE, PhysX, Havok — five engines compared side by side on a shared model
success_criterion: largest timestep h for which the object remains in the hand during the entire simulation (grasp-stability test)
headline_metric: grasp-stability timestep (largest h holding the grasp)
headline_value: MuJoCo Euler and RK tied at 16 ms; PhysX 2 ms; ODE 0.25 ms; Bullet 0.03 ms (Havok excluded, no working PD controller) — Sec. IV-D
note_gaps: Fig. 3's Grasp-row raw-speed (kHz) numbers are OCR-ambiguous (interleaved with accuracy-plot values) and flagged by the note as unreliable to quote directly; Fig. 5's absolute wall-clock scaling numbers for the large-N sparse-solver test did not survive parsing (only the 76x dense-vs-sparse ratio and qualitative 'about 2x slower than gaming engines' claim are given).
